source.label: Source
source.what: A light source: a fan of rays and, with "gauss": true, a Gaussian beam whose diffracted field can be shown.
source.angle: the direction the light leaves in (0 = travelling +x).

fields.meaning: mm: the full width of the ray fan (follows the beam when gauss is true).
degrees, full angle of the fan; negative converges.
true for a Gaussian beam: then set w0 and z0.
mm: how far ahead of the source the waist is (negative: behind it).
grid points for the field: 128, 256, 512 or 1024.
"unpolarised", "s" (out of the bench plane), "p" (in the plane) or "linear" (then polAngle).
extra wavelengths in nm, up to 12.
number of rays in the fan, 1 to 501 (use 1 to 11 with gauss).
coherence length in mm, with cmode "line"; 0 for a single frequency.
id of another source this one is split from (same laser, so they interfere); null for a laser of its own.
degrees of phase against the source it is split from.
mm of extra fibre before this launch, against the other.
"lorentz" or "gauss": the laser line’s shape, with coh.
"single" (one frequency: every path interferes), "line" (a line of its own, from coh and lineshape) or "broad" (incoherent, broadband light of bandwidth bw: only near-equal paths interfere).
bandwidth in nm (FWHM), with cmode "broad": the coherence length is wavelength² / bw.

"gauss" (TEM00), "hg" (a Hermite–Gauss mode HG_mn) or "lg" (a Laguerre–Gauss mode LG_pl, a vortex of charge l when l ≠ 0), built on a Gaussian of waist w0; a higher-order mode uses the 2D field model and ignores m2.
HG m: nodes across the beam in the bench plane, 0–10.
HG n: nodes out of the bench plane, 0–10.
LG l: vortex charge, −10 to 10; its phase is a delay of l·theta/2π waves, as a vortex mask of charge l writes it.
fs: a mode-locked laser’s pulse duration (intensity FWHM at its transform limit); 0 for a continuous laser. Its bandwidth then sets coh.
MHz: the repetition rate (power is the average power).
fs²: the chirp the pulse leaves the laser with (0 at its transform limit).
optional {"core": µm, "na": NA}: a launch from a single-mode fibre, which sets w0 and z0 itself.

mirror.label: Mirror
mirror.what: A mirror, flat or curved (spherical or conic), partly transmitting if reflect < 100.
mirror.angle: the direction its reflecting face points (its normal, towards the light it reflects).

fields.meaning: mm: the mirror’s width across the bench.
mm: an off-axis segment of the parent surface, this far from its vertex.
mm radius of curvature, null for flat. Positive: concave towards the light it faces (focuses, f = R/2); negative: convex.
fs² added to each reflection (a chirped mirror; negative compresses a pulse); 0 for an ordinary mirror.
"lin" or "log": the irradiance map of the light arriving (its Diffraction tab, as a screen’s).
"auto", "on" or "off": the vector focus model for steep beams arriving.
lp/mm at which its Diffraction tab quotes the MTF.

lens.label: Lens
lens.what: A lens of any number of surfaces (singlet, doublet, asphere, cylinder, axicon) in real glass.
lens.angle: the direction of its optical axis. Surface 1 is on the side the axis points away from: at angle 0 light travelling +x meets surfaces[0] first.

fields.meaning: list of surfaces in the order the light meets them at angle 0, each {"R": mm or null for flat, "k": conic, "A": [aspheric a4, a6, …], "coat": coating}. Standard sign convention: R > 0 has its centre of curvature on the far side (downstream).
mm: centre thicknesses between successive surfaces (one fewer than surfaces).
optional: "plane" for a cylindrical lens with power in the bench plane, "out" for power out of it.

screen.label: Screen
screen.what: A screen: records the rays and the field arriving on its face, and gives spot size, profile, PSF, MTF, Strehl and more.
screen.angle: the direction its face points: towards the light it records.

fields.meaning: mm: the width of its face.
mm: a curved screen; negative puts its centre of curvature on the side the light comes from (like a retina); null for flat.
mm for the binned intensity; 0 chooses.
true interpolates the rays into the bins.
"auto", "on" or "off": the vector focus model for steep beams.

"none", an atom ("Rb87", "Rb85", "Cs133", "K39", "Na23") or "sphere" (a dielectric sphere) to read an optical trap for near this screen (the Trap tab): where it sits, depth, trap frequencies each way and scattering, from every beam through the screen’s region.

for atoms, the ground hyperfine level they are in: "avg" (the centroid), "lo" or "hi" (F = I ∓ 1/2); it moves the lines by a few GHz, which matters close to them (the tune-out wavelength between D1 and D2 moves by picometres).
the sphere’s glass ("Fused silica", "Polystyrene" and so on).
"bench" (the index where the light is: put the focus in a block of "Water" for a liquid), "vacuum" or "air" (with trapP).
air pressure, mbar: sets the gas damping and quality factors.
temperature (K): the depth in kT and the gas.
lp/mm at which the MTF is quoted.
the id of the fan source the Aberrations tab sweeps across the field ("" for the first reaching the screen).
its largest field angle, degrees, for a collimated source.
its largest object height, mm, for a diverging source (a point object).
rays in each field’s fan, odd, 11 to 401.

stop.label: Stop
stop.what: An aperture: iris, slit, double slit, slit comb, knife edge or beam block.
stop.angle: its normal: 0 for a beam travelling ±x (the blades then lie along y).

fields.meaning: mm: the opening (an iris’s diameter, a slit’s width).
mm: the outer size (a beam block’s diameter).
one of the stop shapes below.
mm: a double slit’s centre-to-centre separation.
a comb’s number of slits, 2 to 400.
mm: the opening’s centre along the stop.
mm: a slit’s height out of the plane (0 unlimited).
1 or −1: which side a knife edge covers.

cube.label: Beam splitter cube
cube.what: A beam-splitter cube: non-polarising ("npbs", reflect %) or polarising ("pbs", reflectS/reflectP %).
cube.angle: turns its internal diagonal. At 0 the diagonal runs like "/": light travelling +x reflects to +y, travelling −x reflects to −y, and it transmits straight on. At 90 the diagonal is "\": +x reflects to −y.

fields.meaning: coating on its outer faces (see Coatings).

prism.label: Prism
prism.angle: rotates the prism about its centre; check the result on the bench.

fields.meaning: one of the prism shapes below.

waveplate.label: Waveplate
waveplate.angle: its normal: 0 for a beam travelling ±x.

fields.meaning: retardance in waves (0.25 quarter-wave, 0.5 half-wave, or any value).
degrees: the fast axis from p.

polariser.label: Polariser
polariser.angle: its normal: 0 for a beam travelling ±x.

fields.meaning: degrees: the transmission axis from p (0 passes p, 90 passes s).

mask.label: Mask
mask.what: A thin mask with an amplitude and a delay (in waves) written as formulas: also the way to model an ideal lens or objective.
mask.angle: its normal: 0 for a beam travelling ±x.

fields.meaning: amplitude transmission as a formula in x (mm along the mask), y (mm out of the plane), r, theta, lambda (mm) and pi; e.g. "1" or "circ(r/2)".
delay in waves as a formula in the same variables. An ideal lens of focal length f mm: "-(sqrt(r^2+f^2)-f)/lambda" (write f as a number).

grating.label: Grating
grating.what: A diffraction grating, reflecting or transmitting.
grating.angle: the direction its ruled face points (like a mirror for mode "reflect").

fields.meaning: % into the first order at the blaze.

fibre.label: Fibre
fibre.what: A fibre tip: takes free-space light into a fibre by mode overlap, and sends a fibre network’s light out.
fibre.angle: the direction its face points: towards the light it takes in, and the way it sends light out. Its fibre port is on the back.

fields.meaning: µm core diameter (mode field set from core and NA).
rays in the fan it sends out, 0 to 51.
true for a multimode fibre (give it core 50 or 62.5 and na 0.22): it takes in what lands on its core inside its NA, and sends out a beam filling core and NA.

detector.label: Photodetector
detector.what: A free-space photodiode with an amplifier: DC, beat notes, RF spectrum, oscilloscope trace and a mixer output.
detector.angle: the direction its face points: towards the light.

fields.meaning: one of the detector materials below.
MHz: mix the output down at this frequency (0: no mixer). With an EOM at fm, this gives a PDH error signal.

faraday.label: Faraday rotator
faraday.angle: its normal, and the direction of its magnetic field: the sense of rotation depends on the direction of travel against it.

isolator.label: Optical isolator
isolator.what: An optical isolator (polariser, 45° Faraday rotator, polariser).
isolator.angle: its forward direction: light travelling along the angle passes, light travelling against it is blocked.

fields.meaning: degrees: the input polariser from p.

stl.label: STL object
stl.what: An STL object: an opaque shape brought in from a .stl file (a mount, a housing, a baffle), every ray that meets it stopped where it lands, as a beam block. Its triangles ("mesh") are written by JEKray2D when the person imports the file; you cannot write one, so leave STL objects out of the file and tell the person to bring theirs in with Open ▾ → Import an object (.stl), or drop the file on the bench.
stl.angle: the way the object’s own +x (as in its file) points; its tip and roll turn it as any part’s.

fields.meaning: its triangles, written by the tool when a .stl file is imported: leave it out.
mm per unit of the file, with "units": "other".

crystal.label: Crystal
crystal.what: A birefringent crystal: beam displacer, Wollaston prism or Glan–Taylor polariser.
crystal.angle: the direction of its entrance face’s normal (0 for light travelling ±x).

fields.meaning: one of the crystal shapes below.
degrees: the optic axis from the normal, for a displacer.
degrees: the wedge angle, for Wollaston and Glan–Taylor.

filter.label: Filter
filter.what: A filter: long-pass, short-pass, band-pass or neutral density, optionally reflecting what it rejects (a dichroic).
filter.angle: its normal: 0 for a beam travelling ±x.

fields.meaning: one of the filter types below.
nm: the edge of a long- or short-pass.
nm: the 10–90% width of the edge.
optical density of an "nd" filter: it transmits 10^−od.
true: what it rejects is reflected (a dichroic) rather than absorbed.

gain.label: Gain medium
gain.what: A thin gain medium with a Lorentzian gain line that saturates: in a cavity above threshold the laser settles at its output power and the output leaves each partly transmitting mirror as a beam.
gain.angle: its normal: 0 for a beam travelling ±x.

fields.meaning: mm: its aperture across the beam (it is a thin sheet).
small-signal single-pass power gain at the line centre (×); the pump sets it.

kW/cm² saturation intensity (Nd:YAG 2.9, Ti:sapphire 200, Yb:YAG 10); 0: no saturation. Above threshold the cavity settles at the power where the saturated gain balances the loss, and the output leaves each partly transmitting mirror as a beam.

cell.label: Vapour cell
cell.what: An atomic vapour cell (Rb, Cs or K; D1 or D2): Doppler-broadened hyperfine absorption and dispersion at the light’s frequency, and saturated absorption (Lamb dips and crossovers) for a weak beam crossing a strong one going the other way. Set a source’s wavelength to the line in vacuum nm (Rb D2 780.24, Cs D2 852.35).
cell.angle: its axis: 0 for a beam travelling ±x (the cell lies along x).

fields.meaning: mm along the beam (75 is usual).
°C: sets the vapour density (25 for room temperature; heat a potassium cell to about 60).
gauss, a magnetic field along the cell (+ along its angle): Zeeman-split sigma+ and sigma- lines, so circular dichroism (DAVLL) and Faraday rotation (Faraday filters). 0 for none.

nlc.label: Nonlinear crystal
nlc.what: A periodically poled nonlinear crystal (MgO:PPLN or PPKTP) that doubles the frequency of light polarised along its z axis: the second harmonic leaves as a beam of its own, from Boyd and Kleinman’s theory for the focusing, the poling period and the temperature, and the fundamental leaves depleted. Put a lens before it so the beam focuses in its middle.
nlc.angle: its axis: 0 for a beam travelling ±x (the crystal lies along x).

fields.meaning: mm: the aperture across the beam.
mm along the beam (10 to 50 is usual).
poling period, µm; 0 (the default) picks the best period for the beam through it.
°C: tunes the phase matching (PPLN is usually run hot, 40 to 200).
"s" (z axis out of the bench plane: s light converts) or "p".
"ar" (end faces anti-reflection coated, 0.1%; the default) or "bare".

link.label: Link plane
link.what: One of a pair of link planes joining two tabs: the pair is one plane seen from two benches.
link.angle: its normal. Light crossing one plane of a pair leaves its partner (on another tab) the same way relative to that plane.

fields.meaning: the pair’s name: exactly two link planes share it, one on each tab.

aom.label: Acousto-optic modulator
aom.what: A free-space acousto-optic modulator: shifts the diffracted order by the drive frequency.
aom.angle: its normal: 0 for a beam travelling ±x. Order +1 turns the beam anticlockwise by asin(λ·rf/v); order −1 clockwise.

fields.meaning: MHz drive: the order is shifted by this.
m/s sound speed (4200 for TeO₂ shear is typical of fibre AOMs; 650 slow shear).

eom.label: Electro-optic modulator
eom.what: A free-space electro-optic modulator: phase (sidebands) or amplitude modulation.
eom.angle: its normal: 0 for a beam travelling ±x.

chopper.label: Optical chopper
chopper.what: An optical chopper: a slotted wheel across the beam, open for the first part of each cycle; photodetectors behind it see the chopped light (the bench draws it open).
chopper.angle: its blade’s normal: 0 (or 180) across a beam travelling along x, as a stop.

fields.meaning: degrees: when in the cycle it opens, against t = 0 (0: opens at t = 0).

draw.label: Drawing
draw.what: A drawing for figures: a rectangle, an ellipse, a path of Bézier curves or a text, filled and stroked like an SVG shape. The light passes through it as if it were not there. Its shape is in its own frame, centred on x, y.
draw.angle: turns the drawing about its x, y.

fields.meaning: "under" the beams and parts, or "over" them.
mm, an ellipse’s radius along x.
mm, an ellipse’s radius along y.

a path’s nodes, [{"x": mm, "y": mm, "h1": [dx, dy] or null, "h2": [dx, dy] or null}], from x, y; h1 and h2 are the Bézier handles into and out of the node, from it (null: a straight piece). "smooth": true keeps a node’s handles in line when one is dragged.
true joins a path’s last node to its first.
a text’s words; \n starts a new line. x, y is where its first line starts, is centred or ends (align), on its baseline.
optional [a, b, c, d]: a skew (or scale) on the shape before its angle, x′ = a x + c y, y′ = b x + d y; left out, none.
Polarisation angle from s (°), for pol "linear"
